candidates.title: Age, speed limits for e-scooters and other personal electric vehicles hitting Manitoba roads next year
candidates.description: Riders must be at least 16 years old and anyone using the devices, including passengers, are required to wear properly fitting helmets, the province says. Personal electric vehicles can't go faster than 25 km/h under the incoming speed limit.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Support floods in for Gus, Halifax's 104-year-old gopher tortoise, ahead of surgery
candidates.description: Hundreds of get-well messages and art pieces have been sent to the tortoise before he undergoes a bladder surgery on Tuesday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Could Quebec's new government derail plans for Alto's high-speed train project?
candidates.description: The Crown corporation responsible for a proposed high-speed rail line connecting Toronto to Quebec City says it plans to deliver on the project, despite opposition from the newly elected Parti Québécois (PQ) government.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'Disrespect for wildlife': Multiple grizzly bear poaching incidents under investigation in Alberta
candidates.description: Provincial officials are investigating the illegal killings of four grizzly bears at three separate locations over the last year. One of the bear corpses was found abandoned with its paws removed after being poached.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: How some separatists are responding to Smith’s pledge against 2nd referendum if remain vote wins
candidates.description: Premier Danielle Smith’s pledge that she won’t hold another referendum on separation if the remain vote wins this month — at least as long as she is premier — is getting pushback from some prominent Alberta separatists.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Why this Fredericton woman is walking a Ukrainian battalion flag across P.E.I.
candidates.description: Julia Cardy will spend two weeks walking across Prince Edward Island with a flag her friend April Huggett carried for 700 kilometres in Ukraine. The journey is raising money for Ukrainian soldiers and bringing their stories closer to home.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: After 20 years as a P.E.I. firefighter, something snapped. Now he's teaching others about PTSD
candidates.description: Ernie Gallant was diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder after dedicating two decades of volunteer service to the New Glasgow Fire Department in Prince Edward Island.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: ‘Every rock has a story’: retired geologist opens rock library in Whitehorse
candidates.description: Tucked away down a quiet street in Whitehorse is a new community library, with a geological twist. You won't find a new thriller, or a well-loved cookbook. The shelves aren’t filled with paper, they’re filled with rocks.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Man admits to 5 sex assaults near Winnipeg's Health Sciences Centre, including one against 14-year-old girl
candidates.description: A man charged in five sexual assaults near Winnipeg's Health Sciences Centre last summer has pleaded guilty. Donovan Mohammed sat quietly in the prisoner's box Friday, speaking briefly to confirm to his lawyer he was admitting guilt.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: New church set to rise up after 'suspicious' fire in Kinngait, Nunavut
candidates.description: More than three years after a suspicious fire destroyed the Anglican church in Kinngait, Nunavut, work is well underway to begin building a new structure.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Disappointed, angry, excited: Albertans weigh in on looming referendum
candidates.description: At a library branch CBC News visited in Calgary, a few people were excited to vote. Others were just starting to follow the process, and several expressed frustration at Alberta even having a referendum.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Woman who married ISIS fighter pleads guilty to terror-related charge
candidates.description: Kimberly Polman pleaded guilty on Thursday to leaving Canada to participate in activities of a terrorist group, namely the Islamic State in Iraq and Syria (ISIS).
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Ex-Marineland beluga whale dies in Chicago aquarium
candidates.description: Shedd Aquarium in Chicago says Caspian, a 27-year-old female beluga, died on Wednesday, becoming the sixth animal from the closed Ontario theme park Marineland to die after a massive relocation of whales and dolphins over the summer.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 'You're Russian now': Ukrainians raised in Crimea share how Russia trained them to become future soldiers
candidates.description: Three Ukrainians who grew up in occupied Crimea describe how Russia trained them to become future soldiers for its war on Ukraine, including school classes on how to handle weapons — part of a larger pattern of Russian indoctrination of children that has raised alarm in the international community.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Children among at least 139 dead after migrant boat capsizes off Djibouti coast
candidates.description: At least 139 people, including children, have died after a boat carrying more than 300 migrants capsized off the coast of Djibouti in East Africa, the International Organization for Migration said Sunday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Hurricane Simon hits Mexico's Pacific coast, slamming towns and resorts
candidates.description: Hurricane Simon was pounding Mexico's Pacific coast as a Category 4 storm on Sunday, its eye remaining just offshore as its most powerful winds and rain slammed people living between the Sierra Madre and the ocean.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Saudi-led coalition vows retaliation after deadly Houthi attack on Riyadh airport
candidates.description: At least ‌12 ​people were killed ​and 309 others ​were injured in a ‌Saturday attack on King Khalid International ‌Airport in Riyadh, ​the Saudi Civil Aviation Authority said on ​Sunday.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump announces Russia-Ukraine 'energy ceasefire,' which Zelenskyy says he hasn't seen but supports
candidates.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he has discussed the possibility of an energy ceasefire with Russia with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, Finnish President Alex Stubb and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte but is waiting for more information from the United States.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Pope Leo will undergo surgery to remove a nodule on his lung
candidates.description: Pope Leo announced Sunday he will undergo surgery in the coming days to remove a nodular lesion on his lung that was recently discovered during medical checks.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: What happens when a Google data centre comes to town? Southern India is finding out
candidates.description: India is vying to secure a piece of the AI boom, and letting Google clear hundreds of acres to build a $15 billion US data centre hub near its eastern coast. It will be the company's largest such project outside the U.S., and comes with promises of jobs and investments. But at what cost?
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Panama declares state of emergency as powerful quake aftershocks rattle communities
candidates.description: The government of Panama declared a state of emergency Saturday as the aftershocks of two powerful earthquakes that roiled the country shook communities for hours. Officials did not attribute any deaths to the quakes but reported damages in all 10 of Panama's provinces and two Indigenous territories.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump says Ukraine should get a new president, blames Zelenskyy for U.S. diesel prices
candidates.description: U.S. President Donald Trump says it's time for Ukraine to get a new president, suggesting current Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has not done enough to end his country's war with Russia.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Villages evacuated as flash flood from Budhi Gandaki river hits northern Nepal
candidates.description: Residents along the Budhi Gandaki river in north central Nepal evacuated on Sunday as flash flooding destroyed homes and other structures in the area.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Category 4 Hurricane Simon barrels toward Mexico
candidates.description: Hurricane Simon ​strengthened into a powerful Category 4 storm off Mexico's Pacific coast on Saturday, threatening destructive winds, storm surges and potentially deadly flooding as it approaches landfall.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: 4 dead, hundreds of thousands without power as Isaias weakens
candidates.description: Isaias left behind a trail of damaged rooftops, downed power lines and flooded roadways Saturday as it weakened and was no longer a hurricane. It was blamed for at least four deaths.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Netanyahu faces fresh allegations he ignored warnings about Oct. 7 — right before an election
candidates.description: Just weeks before a potentially pivotal election, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is defending against new allegations that he ignored high-level warnings from Arab allies that might have prevented the Hamas-led attacks on Oct. 7, 2023.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Children, pregnant woman among 9 dead in Pennsylvania shooting
candidates.description: A shooting in a residential area of Erie, Pa., left nine people dead, including the suspected shooter, and rocked the city. Police said two children and a pregnant woman were among the dead.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Fish in American fish sticks is fueling a fight over trawling in Alaska
candidates.description: Chum from Bering Sea pollock trawlers have become contentious as salmon runs have collapsed across western Alaska, where dozens of Indigenous communities have relied on salmon for generations. The backlash has spread to smaller commercial and charter fishers who say they, too, are bearing the costs of declining stocks.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: He was ready to fight in the 'war on terror.' This post-9/11 veteran looks back at his decision to enlist
candidates.description: After the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks, CBC’s chief correspondent Adrienne Arsenault reported on young people who enlisted to fight in the global "war on terror." Twenty-four years later, she tracked down one U.S. marine she met to find out if he got what he signed up for.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Trump wants to dismantle the ICC. These jurists want Canada to intervene
candidates.description: After the Trump administration announced sweeping sanctions against the International Criminal Court, Canadian legal professionals are calling on the federal government to take action to strengthen the court through additional funding or other measures.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Christa Pike discharged from hospital after surviving execution attempt, attorney says
candidates.description: Christa Pike, who survived Tennessee's attempt to execute her by lethal injection, has been moved back to prison, according to a statement released by her attorneys.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Anthropic's Claude AI submits a false tip on a Philadelphia unsolved homicide case
candidates.description: An Anthropic artificial intelligence model submitted a false tip to a Philadelphia police website about an unsolved homicide case, authorities and Anthropic said.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: India detains thousands as 'Cockroach' youth movement protests voter list revision
candidates.description: Indian authorities deployed a sweeping security crackdown across New Delhi and detained thousands of protesters Saturday as India’s youth "Cockroach" movement sought to intensify a nationwide campaign against a contentious voter list revision that has fuelled anger at Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Hindu nationalist government and election authorities.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Stelco says Hamilton layoffs still happening despite Ottawa's threats of legal action
candidates.description: Hamilton-based steelmaker Stelco says it will proceed with hundreds of layoffs, despite threats of legal action from the federal government.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: AI photos are making it harder to know what you're booking on Airbnb. Here's what to look out for
candidates.description: Josh Wells was excited to explore Montreal on his first trip outside the U.S. But as he scrolled through listings on Airbnb, he noticed something odd: Several host profile pictures and one listing had what appeared to be AI-generated pictures.
candidates.author: CBC News

candidates.title: Saudi capital airport hit by second Houthi strike in two days
candidates.description: The Yemeni group says it carried out attacks that killed 13 people in Riyadh over the weekend and targeted two airports and oil facilities.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Ukraine strikes Yandex data centre in third attack on Russian tech giant
candidates.description: It is the third time this week that Ukraine has targeted Russian tech giant Yandex, forcing the company to suspend its operations.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Homes and bridges swept away as fresh floods hit Nepal
candidates.description: Nepal is still trying to recover from catastrophic floods that hit less than two months ago, leaving thousands dead and missing.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Poland stabbings driven by online glorification of violence, Tusk says
candidates.description: The PM was speaking after violent attacks at Polish schools this week left one dead and others injured.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Children among 139 dead after boat capsizes off Djibouti, UN says
candidates.description: The boat was travelling from Djibouti to Yemen with 305 people on board, when it capsized near the port town of Obock on Thursday night.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: US justice department investigates TV networks over Trump pool coverage
candidates.description: The White House had blocked access for CNN, MS Now and Politico, leading them to restrict pool coverage.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Expedition hopes to find aviator Amelia Earhart's plane on remote island
candidates.description: The team en route to the suspected crash site aim finally to solve the mystery of her 1937 disappearance.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: US murderer Christa Pike discharged from hospital 10 days after failed execution
candidates.description: Pike's lawyers say she is "grateful" to the medical team who cared for her after she survived two lethal injections last month.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Headmaster detained after BBC investigation into alleged sexual abuse of students
candidates.description: Former students launched their own investigation, spending years collecting evidence and testimonies from others who say they were abused by the headteacher.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Woman injures three people in third Poland school knife attack in a week
candidates.description: Polish police had already deployed to schools after a female caretaker was killed and several others injured in two earlier attacks in two days.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Riyadh airport attacks another dangerous moment in already tense conflict
candidates.description: While the physical damage from Houthi attacks can be quickly repaired, the Saudi reputation for stability is taking a battering.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Public executions in the US stopped nearly a century ago - why are they resuming now?
candidates.description: The Pentagon says the execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan will be livestreamed, but experts suggest officials are reading the country wrong.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Nord Stream trial: How German police followed the evidence - to Ukraine
candidates.description: After four years, a Ukrainian man is set to stand trial in Hamburg accused of sabotaging the Nord Stream pipelines.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Buildings swept away as flash floods hit central Nepal
candidates.description: A flash flood at the Budhi Gandaki River has swept away several buildings and bridges, two months after catastrophic floods hit the country.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Why have hundreds of 'cockroach' protesters been detained in Delhi
candidates.description: Thousands of security personnel were deployed in Delhi ahead of the Gen-Z led Cockroach Janta Party protest on Saturday calling for electoral reforms.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How the trial of murdered Australian brothers and US friend unfolded
candidates.description: The mother of two Australian surfers murdered in Mexico two years ago with their American friend said "accountability matters".
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: King warns malicious online actors are evolving tactics
candidates.description: The King spoke of "threats to our international order" in a letter marking the 10th anniversary of the National Cyber Security Centre.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Rogue Anthropic AI agent gave police fake tip in unsolved murder case
candidates.description: Philadelphia police said the tip was "flagged as spam", but criticised the tech company for taking more than two months to detect and report the breach.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: How drones are hunting fires hidden beneath the Cairngorms
candidates.description: Dramatic flames from the huge Cairngorms wildfire in July have disappeared - but hot spots can continue to burn beneath the earth.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Four dead and thousands without power after Hurricane Isaias lashes US
candidates.description: Roofs were ripped off buildings after Isaias barrelled into the US on Friday evening, before it weakened to a post-tropical cyclone.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: Hurricane Isaias downgraded after making landfall in Florida
candidates.description: Hundreds of thousands of households are without power in Florida and Alabama as Isaias continues its path across south-eastern US.
candidates.author: BBC News

candidates.title: She was a global star: Teen bikes 700 miles carrying injured dad. Where is she now?
candidates.description: Her epic ride — carrying her injured dad on her $20 hot pink bicycle — made headlines. Promises were made — financial help, training for a cycling career, even a movie deal. Were any of them kept?
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Passenger terminal at Riyadh airport is struck again, a day after 12 were killed
candidates.description: A projectile struck a passenger terminal at the international airport in Riyadh on Sunday, a day after a missile hit the same terminal and killed 12 people, officials said.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Bayeux Tapestry's London tour spurs enthusiasts to Battle of Hastings reenactment
candidates.description: A reenactment of the Battle of Hastings, which took place almost a millennium ago, is drawing crowds of enthusiasts in the UK.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Trump weighs joining the fight against Houthis after Riyadh airport attack
candidates.description: The surge in attacks, including against other Saudi airports, military facilities and oil infrastructure, has come in the week since a Saudi-led coalition launched a major military offensive against the Houthis.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Protests against voter roll revisions rock capital of world's largest democracy
candidates.description: Parts of the capital city of India, the world's largest democracy, are on lockdown. Protests over sweeping revisions to the voter rolls were met with a massive police crackdown.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: U.S. and Russia tout diesel deal to ease sanctions and reopen fuel flows
candidates.description: Moscow and Washington tout a diesel deal to ease sanctions and reopen fuel flows, but few details leave questions on price impacts and U.S. policy, sparking anger from Ukraine and allies.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Photos: What a year of ceasefire in Gaza looks like
candidates.description: It has been one year since Hamas released the remaining Israeli hostages and President Trump promised an end to the war, but Palestinians say the past 12 months have been a ceasefire in name only.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: India cracks down on youth protests as anger grows against Modi and election chief
candidates.description: The protests focus on the Election Commission's voter list revision, which the opposition claims disenfranchises millions. The government denies the allegations, saying the revision aims to eliminate duplicate entries.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: South African human rights lawyer Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize
candidates.description: South African human rights lawyer Navi Pillay wins the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her lifelong defense of human rights and international law.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Justice Department investigates TV networks, citing possible anti-trust violations
candidates.description: The move escalates Trump's fight with the press amid court battle over barring CNN, Politico and MS NOW from the White House.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: It's taking longer to find a new job after losing one
candidates.description: People who lose their jobs in this economy are taking longer to find new work. Nearly four in ten people exhaust their unemployment benefits before they land a new job.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Kalshi taps former FBI agent to fight against money laundering
candidates.description: The prediction market company says it wants to prevent its platform from being abused by criminals. The company is facing mounting pressure over market manipulation and insider trading on the site.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Fired OpenAI employees question the company's commitment to safety
candidates.description: The three fired workers say OpenAI punished them for being outspoken about safety. The company disputes the claims and says they were fired over mishandling sensitive information.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How the beverage aisle got so wild
candidates.description: Planet Money traced many new beverage flavors to one laboratory that serves dozens of companies to see how new flavors are created and why we're seeing such an explosion of options right now.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: How one antibiotic morning-after pill came to be widely available in San Francisco
candidates.description: An antibiotic morning-after pill has been shown to be effective for preventing STIs among gay men, but some doctors worry about antibiotic resistance. This story discusses STIs and their symptoms.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Don't be scared: Being afraid is outright fun, and maybe useful
candidates.description: Listeners of NPR's Weekend Edition Sunday may already know that host Ayesha Rascoe loves horror. But why do scream queens (and kings) like her like what's frightening? The answer may surprise you.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Sweating the details: Sauna's potential health benefits draw scientists' interest
candidates.description: A group of international researchers is pushing to rigorously study the potential health benefits of sauna and other heat therapies. They hope to bring scientific legitimacy to the age-old practices.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.title: Ongoing lawsuits allege GLP-1s can cause serious harm. But we don't know how often
candidates.description: Scant data about serious adverse effects makes it harder to answer scientific and legal questions about how often the drugs might cause serious harm like blindness or pancreatitis.
candidates.author: NPR

candidates.description: The United States Geological Survey reported an earthquake of magnitude 6.6. The event occurred near 14 km W of Río Grande, Panama. Official monitoring data may be updated as scientists review additional measurements.
